active_subtask: Phase F: profiled the baseline NPU run (no MTP). Decode-phase storage re-reads are catastrophic (85-308GiB re-read depending on generation length, confirmed across three runs). Measured per-layer locality at two window lengths per user's choice (option 3): short window (63 calls) showed modest LRU hit rates (30-46%); longer window (127 calls) roughly DOUBLED hit rates at every K (50-72%) -- the cache needs time to warm up, and short windows understated its potential. This is a measured, not assumed, revised (more favorable) expected payoff. Next: proceed with the Phase 1 bounded-slot-cache implementation given this improved data, or test a narrower-domain prompt (e.g. code-generation) for completeness first -- awaiting user decision.

Phase C: ran -dev HTP0 --n-cpu-moe 48 (all MoE forced to CPU, isolating whether crash is MoE-specific) with full instrumentation -- NO Scudo crash this time, but captured a DIFFERENT failure: process RSS ballooned from 19MB to 6.2GB in ~10 seconds (measured via 1s-interval ps samples), available RAM crashed to ~15MB, swap exploded from 1.0GB to 5GB -- a genuine OOM/thrashing death spiral, not heap corruption

Phase C: root-caused via source inspection: llama-model.cpp:1512-1519 disables mmap for the ENTIRE model if ANY device in -dev reports mmap_support=false under AUTO load-mode; ggml-hexagon.cpp:7517 hardcodes mmap_support=false (vs ggml-cpu.cpp's true). This means -dev HTP0 alone (regardless of --n-cpu-moe) forces eager full-file read instead of lazy paging -- explaining the RSS explosion precisely. Likely also explains the earlier Scudo aborts as a downstream symptom of the same memory exhaustion.

Phase C: FIX VERIFIED LIVE with full logcat+mem-monitor+watchdog safety net: -dev HTP0 -lm mmap --n-cpu-moe 48 (forcing mmap explicitly bypasses the AUTO-only disable check) completed cleanly -- load 10.1s, prompt eval 4.00 tok/s, decode eval 2.46 tok/s (better than CPU-only baseline's 1.21 tok/s), memory stable throughout (free 650-760MB, available 5.5GB, peak RSS ~6.1GB but no thrashing). Output was incoherent at this run's settings (temp=0 greedy, no repeat-penalty) -- expected per the earlier coherence findings, orthogonal to the crash fix. -lm mmap is now a REQUIRED flag whenever -dev HTP0 is used.

Phase C: --n-cpu-moe sweep via llama-bench (-dev HTP0 -lm mmap, -p 64 -n 16 -r 1 -b 128 -ub 128 -fa off): n-cpu-moe=48 -> pp64=7.95, tg16=1.33. n-cpu-moe=24 -> pp64=7.99, tg16=2.22. n-cpu-moe=0 -> pp64=8.28, tg16=2.30 (best). 1.24x prompt / 1.90x decode speedup over the CPU-only baseline (6.69/1.21). known_issues.what: --spec-type draft-mtp is functionally real (loads, drafts execute, produces correct/coherent substantive output while running) but exhibits an apparent race condition in OpenMP thread-pool / draft-verify handling under multi-threaded CPU execution (-dev none -t 2 or -t 6). Manifests probabilistically, more likely over longer generations (more draft/verify cycles = more chances to hit it): seen as 'OMP: Error #132: Thread identifier invalid' repeated then Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT) in a worker thread, and separately as Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at a near-null address (fault addr 0x10) before any token was generated. Short generations (-n 16, -n 24) completed cleanly multiple times at -t 1, -t 2, and -t 6; a longer one (-n 48) at the identical -t 6 config crashed. Disabling reasoning mode (-rea off) was initially thought to fix it but does NOT reliably -- it only reduced the window in which the race was observed to trigger.
known_issues.status: NOT ROOT-CAUSED. Not a simple flag-tuning fix -- would need a debug/ASAN build and source-level investigation of how the MTP draft context's thread pool interacts with the main context's thread pool. Logged and not pursued further via live-fire trial-and-error, consistent with how the unrelated exit-time-scudo-abort issue was handled.
known_issues.implication_for_npu_test: RESOLVED (favorably): tested -dev HTP0 -lm mmap --n-cpu-moe 0 + --spec-type draft-mtp at the exact generation length (-n 48) that reliably crashed on CPU-only. Zero crashes across short and long runs, correct/coherent output, memory stable (available pinned ~7.0GB). The race appears specific to the CPU-only (-dev none) threadpool path -- offloading most compute to Hexagon leaves far less concurrent CPU-side work, avoiding it. This is the current best-known-good MTP configuration.

known_issues.what: Intermittent, non-deterministic heap-corruption-on-exit: llama-completion, llama-bench, and llama-cli (all binaries sharing common/libllama-common and the Hexagon backend's static teardown code) occasionally abort with Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), 'Scudo ERROR: invalid chunk state when deallocating', AFTER their normal output (benchmark row, generated text, --help text) has already printed. Confirmed via logcat crash-dump context that this fires even on a bare `llama-completion --help` call (no model, no device, 1s process uptime) -- proving it is unrelated to this model, to -dev HTP0, or to the -lm mmap fix. Most likely a destructor-ordering or double-free bug in shared startup/teardown code, probabilistically detected by Scudo depending on heap layout/reuse timing at exit -- which is why many earlier runs showed no crash at all (absence of a detected abort is not proof the corruption didn't occur, just that it wasn't caught that time).
known_issues.status: NOT BLOCKING -- logged and deliberately not investigated further per explicit user instruction ("continue as if it doesn't exist" unless it recurs/becomes blocking). Output captured before the crash (sweep benchmark numbers, ngram-simple generation) is still considered valid, since the abort happens during teardown after the relevant data was already written.
known_issues.revisit_if: This becomes blocking, affects a long-running process (e.g. a server), or someone wants to file an upstream llama.cpp issue -- would need a debug/ASAN build to actually pin down which destructor/free is at fault.

failed_attempts.what: Any invocation of llama-completion, llama-bench, or test-backend-ops with -dev HTP0 / -b HTP0 against the real qwen3next model (IQ1_S REAP-40B-A3B GGUF) on the Hexagon backend built at pin e358d591.
failed_attempts.error: CONFIRMED via `logcat -d -b main -b system -b crash -b events`: every one of these processes died with Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT) and abort message 'Scudo ERROR: invalid chunk state when deallocating address 0x...' -- this is Android's hardened allocator detecting HEAP CORRUPTION (a bad/already-freed pointer), not out-of-memory. 100% reproducible across 11+ separate attempts from 06:43 to 07:07 (pids 18179, 18232, 19894, 20364, 20680, 25360, 32528, 32614, 7633, 13467, 13640, 14171, 14434, 14971). Initially misdiagnosed by the assistant as a generic device/memory-pressure 'crash' -- logcat evidence corrected this. KEY ISOLATING FACT: a standalone `test-backend-ops -b HTP0` run with only small synthetic matrices (examples/npu-matrix-cases.txt, no real model) passed clean (8/8 OK, no abort) right after the ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH fix. The corruption appears specifically when the real model's tensors (qwen3next: MoE MUL_MAT_ID + hybrid full-attention/linear-recurrent layers) run through the experimental Hexagon backend -- not a RAM-capacity issue tunable via batch size.
failed_attempts.hardware_context: S24 Ultra, 10GiB total RAM. Not fixed by reducing -ngl, -b/-ub, or any resource knob tried -- this is being treated as a likely memory-safety bug in ggml-hexagon.cpp (explicitly logged as 'Hexagon backend (experimental)') when combined with this architecture, not a tuning problem.
failed_attempts.do_not_repeat: RESOLVED 2026-10-08T07:40Z: root cause found and fixed, see completed_steps. ggml-hexagon.cpp:7517 hardcodes mmap_support=false; llama-model.cpp's AUTO load-mode logic disables mmap for the entire model when any -dev device lacks mmap support, forcing an eager full-8.4GB-file read that exhausted RAM in ~10s. The earlier Scudo 'invalid chunk state' aborts were almost certainly a symptom of this same RSS explosion, not a separate memory-safety bug. FIX: always pass -lm mmap (--load-mode mmap) explicitly whenever -dev HTP0 is used -- this bypasses the AUTO-only check and was verified live (full logcat+mem-monitor+watchdog instrumentation) to run cleanly with stable memory (free 650-760MB, available pinned 5.5GB throughout, peak process RSS ~6.1GB, zero crashes, zero Scudo errors).

qwen36_moe_locality_long_window.note: Rerun at 96 decode tokens (vs 32) per user's chosen option: hit rates roughly DOUBLED at every K vs the short-window measurement. The short window understated the cache's potential -- it needs time to warm up. Revised expectation: 50-65% hit rate achievable at realistic generation lengths with K=32-64/layer, substantially better than the short-window 30-40% estimate. Window-length sensitivity is now a documented property, not an assumption.

qwen36_moe_locality.note: Real simulated LRU on actual captured per-layer selection sequences (scripts/moe-profile-probe.cpp, custom untruncated cb_eval). Routing is close to uniform-random at this short-window granularity. A realistic RAM-bounded cache (K~32-64/layer) would cut storage re-reads ~30-40%, not eliminate them. Gains plateau hard past K~64 -- even K=192 (75% of all experts) only reaches 46.4% hit rate.

qwen36_moe_profile.note: scripts/moe-profile-probe.cpp, -dev HTP0 mmap, no MTP, /proc-sourced (solid, not estimated). Decode alone re-read ~85GiB from storage for 32 tokens (~8x the 10.59GiB model file) -- RSS shrank monotonically (4.08GB->2.1GB->647MB) despite reading more data each phase, showing the OS page-cache LRU evicts indiscriminately with no expert-aware locality. Motivates the bounded expert-caching design. Expert-selection trace captured (1280 ffn_moe_topk dumps) but PRELIMINARY ONLY -- debug dump truncates to 6/8 ids per call and pools all 40 layers together; not yet a rigorous per-layer locality measurement.

qwen36_npu_mtp_vs_nospec.note: Controlled same-seed (42) comparison, identical config otherwise, -n 48, same prompt. MTP is SLOWER: ~25% slower prompt eval, ~50% slower decode. At this base decode rate (well under 1 tok/s), draft/verify overhead costs more than any acceptance savings. MTP is functionally real and stable (zero crashes) but not a performance win for this model/quant/hardware combination.

npu_prefill_cpu_decode_handoff.status: CORRECTED: ACHIEVABLE, via a different (custom, local, never-upstreamed) technique -- not llama.cpp's generic --prompt-cache session mechanism, which remains confirmed non-functional for recurrent memory (completion.cpp:334). The repo's existing Oct 3-5 Mistral 7B investigation proved an in-process one-way handoff (llama_perf_switch_to_cpu, reports/2026-10-03/patches/npu-prefill-cpu-decode.patch), originally gated to plain Qwen2/Qwen3 KV only. Extended it (llama_memory_recurrent::perf_migrate_cpu + llama_memory_hybrid dispatch + LLM_ARCH_QWEN3NEXT) and verified live: prefill NPU 6.80s/4.71 tok/s, handoff 1.98s (migrated both 6.00MiB KV and 75.38MiB recurrent/SSM-GDN state, zero crashes), decode CPU 18.94s/0.79 tok/s. CAVEAT: decode after handoff is much slower than native full-CPU (0.79 vs 3.30 tok/s at the same thread count) because the handoff uses canonical (non-repacked) CPU weight shadows, not the CPU_REPACK-optimized layout -- consistent with the project's own prior documented tradeoff for Mistral 7B, but apparently much more punishing for this IQ1_S quant. Net: technique works, is not a speed win here.
